etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English myscreaunt, miscreaunt, from Old French mescreant (1080) "mis-believer", present participle of mescreire "to misbelieve" (modern mécroire). Cognate with French mécréant.
senses: Lacking in conscience or moral principles; unscrupulous.
One who has behaved badly, or illegally.
One not restrained by moral principles; an unscrupulous villain.
